notice: SYNTHETIC ROLE-BASED SIMULATION — NOT BASED ON THESE EMPLOYEES' ACTUAL BEHAVIOR OR WORK HISTORY.
scenario_summary: Project Northstar is a fictional 48-hour hackathon to build an offline-tolerant coordination service for imaginary polar research stations. It processes synthetic beacon and supply events, exposes a status dashboard, and contains no real project data.

decisions.statement: Set an architecture boundary around external adapters.
decisions.decision: Set an architecture boundary around external adapters.
decisions.choice: Use ports for storage, clock, and fictional weather dependencies
alternatives: Call vendor-shaped clients from domain handlers
rationale: Ports keep the core deterministic and make offline testing possible
constraints: No network dependency is required for the demo
risks: Too many abstractions can slow a small implementation
decisions.outcome: Synthetic offline integration coverage increased from 62% to 93%.

decisions.statement: Threat-model the command path before finalizing it.
decisions.decision: Threat-model the command path before finalizing it.
decisions.choice: Require authentication, explicit authorization, replay defense, and audit fields
alternatives: Rely on a private demo network
rationale: Layered controls address distinct command-path risks
constraints: All identities and events are fictional
risks: Control complexity can delay the demo if not scoped
decisions.outcome: Synthetic threat tests passed 48 of 48 abuse cases.

decisions.choice: Allocate the two-second p95 budget across ingress, queue, storage, and projection
alternatives: Optimize only after end-to-end latency fails
rationale: Budgets turn a broad target into measurable component constraints
risks: Local optimization may not improve the critical path
decisions.outcome: Synthetic end-to-end p95 improved from 3.4 seconds to 1.6 seconds.

decisions.statement: Prefer reversible technology choices for the hackathon.
decisions.decision: Prefer reversible technology choices for the hackathon.
decisions.choice: Use SQLite and adapter interfaces instead of introducing a remote platform
alternatives: Add a managed distributed store immediately
rationale: The fictional scale fits local storage and the adapter preserves an evolution path
constraints: No Azure calls or token use
risks: SQLite is not the intended answer for a future distributed deployment
decisions.outcome: Synthetic setup time fell from an estimated 45 minutes to 6 minutes while all 32 integration tests passed.
